t.1.210.1: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: He of boundless valor went, one after another, to all the holy tīrthas and sacred sanctuaries in the western regions.
t.1.210.2: Having visited all the sacred fords and holy places that lie by the western sea, he went on to Prabhāsa.
t.1.210.3: Madhusūdana heard that the unconquered Bībhatsu had reached the region of Prabhāsa and was wandering among the sacred fords.
t.1.210.4: Then Mādhava came to Kaunteya, unrecognized by anyone, and there at Prabhāsa Kṛṣṇa and the Pāṇḍava saw each other.
t.1.210.5: Having embraced each other and asked after each other's welfare, the two stayed together in the forest as dear friends, those two seers Nara and Nārāyaṇa.
t.1.210.6: Then Vāsudeva questioned Arjuna about that wandering of his: “For what purpose, Pāṇḍava, do you go about visiting these sacred fords?”
t.1.210.7: Then Arjuna related everything just as it had happened; and having heard it, the lord Vārṣṇeya said, "So it is."
t.1.210.8: Having amused themselves as they wished at Prabhāsa, those two, Kṛṣṇa and the Pāṇḍava, went to the mountain Raivataka to dwell there.
t.1.210.9: Even beforehand, at Kṛṣṇa's command, men had adorned that mountain and brought food there.
t.1.210.10: Arjuna the Pāṇḍava, having accepted everything and enjoyed it, watched the actors and dancers together with Vāsudeva.
t.1.210.11: Having taken leave of them all and having honored them, the greatly splendid Pāṇḍava went to the honored, divine couch.
t.1.210.13: Even as he was telling stories, O Janamejaya, the son of Kuntī was carried off by sleep on that bed equal to heaven.
t.1.210.12: And he told the Sātvata, O Bhārata, of his visits to the sacred fords, and to the mountains, rivers, and forests.
t.1.210.14: Being awakened by sweet song and the sound of the vīṇā, O sinless one, and likewise by hymns of praise and auspicious blessings, he woke up.
t.1.210.15: Having performed the necessary duties and been greeted by Vārṣṇeya, he went to Dvārakā in a chariot with golden parts.
t.1.210.16: Dvārakā was adorned, O Janamejaya, in honor of the son of Kuntī, even in its pleasure-gardens.
t.1.210.17: And the people dwelling in Dvārakā, eager to see the son of Kuntī, swiftly came to the royal highway by hundreds of thousands.
t.1.210.19: Thus honored by all the sons of the Bhojas, Vṛṣṇis, and Andhakas, he saluted those worthy of salutation and was welcomed in return by all.
t.1.210.18: At the lookout places there were hundreds and thousands of women, and a great gathering of the Bhojas, Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas took place.
t.1.210.20: The hero, greeted with honor by the young princes on every side, embraced again and again all those who were of his own age.
t.1.210.21: In Kṛṣṇa's delightful mansion, filled with jewels and things to eat, he dwelt there together with Kṛṣṇa for many nights.
